text: Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 Attendance Rules Document No: SIET/ATT/2026/02 | Effective: Academic Year 2026-27 1. Minimum Attendance Requirement 1.1 A student must have a minimum of 75% attendance in each course (theory and laboratory) to be eligible to write the end-semester examination. 1.2 Attendance is calculated separately for every course as: (Hours attended / Total hours conducted) x 100. 2. Condonation of Shortage Attendance Range Status Requirement 75% and above Eligible None 65% to below 75% Condonation possible Valid reason, medical certificate if applicable, and a condonation fee of Rs. 250 per course Below 65% Not eligible Student must repeat the course in a later semester ("Detained") 1.3 Condonation is allowed a maximum of two times during the entire programme. 1.4 Applications for condonation must be submitted to the HoD within 5 working days after the last instructional day. 3. Attendance Marks (Internal Assessment) Attendance Marks (out of 5) 95% and above 5 90% to below 95% 4 85% to below 90% 3 80% to below 85% 2 75% to below 80%

(Internal Assessment) Attendance Marks (out of 5) 95% and above 5 90% to below 95% 4 85% to below 90% 3 80% to below 85% 2 75% to below 80% 1 4. On-Duty (OD) Attendance 4.1 OD is granted for college-approved activities: sports meets, technical symposiums, paper presentations, and NSS/NCC camps. 4.2 OD requests must be approved by the HoD before the event, and proof of participation must be submitted within 3 days after. 4.3 OD hours are counted as present, with a maximum of 10% of total hours per semester. 5. Late Arrival 5.1 Students arriving more than 10 minutes after the period begins are marked absent for that period. 5.2 Three late arrivals in a month are counted as one full-day absence. 6. Biometric and Proxy Attendance 6.1 Attendance is recorded through the biometric system at the start of the first period and by faculty for subsequent periods.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 2 6.2 Proxy attendance is a serious offence. Both students involved face a fine of Rs. 1,000 and a one-week suspension. 7. Display of Attendance 7.1 Faculty advisors publish attendance monthly. Students can view real-time attendance on the college ERP portal.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 College Regulations Institution: Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) Document No: SIET/REG/2026/01 | Effective: 1 July 2026 | Applies to: All UG and PG students 1. General Conduct 1.1 Students must carry their college ID card at all times on campus and show it on request to staff or security. 1.2 Students must maintain discipline, courtesy, and respect toward faculty, staff, and fellow students. 1.3 Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited and is a punishable offence under UGC regulations and state law. 1.4 Use of mobile phones is not permitted inside classrooms, laboratories, and examination halls. 1.5 Smoking, alcohol, and possession of narcotics are prohibited on campus and within 100 metres of the gate. 2. Dress Code 2.1 Students must wear formal or smart-casual attire on working days. 2.2 Lab sessions require closed footwear. Department-prescribed uniform is mandatory on Wednesdays. 2.3 Sleeveless tops, torn jeans, and slippers are not permitted in academic blocks. 3. Campus Timings - Academic hours: 8:45 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday to

is mandatory on Wednesdays. 2.3 Sleeveless tops, torn jeans, and slippers are not permitted in academic blocks. 3. Campus Timings - Academic hours: 8:45 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday to Friday. - Saturday: 8:45 AM to 1:00 PM (working Saturdays as notified in the academic calendar). - Library: 8:30 AM to 7:00 PM on working days. - Main gate closes at 6:30 PM for day scholars. 4. Use of Campus Facilities 4.1 Computer labs may be used only for academic purposes. Installing unauthorized software is prohibited. 4.2 Damage to college property must be compensated by the student responsible, in addition to disciplinary action. 4.3 Students must book seminar halls through the Head of the Department at least 3 working days in advance. 5. Disciplinary Action Offence Action Minor misconduct (late entry, dress code) Written warning Repeated minor misconduct Fine of Rs. 500 and parent intimation Damage to property Recovery of cost plus a fine up to Rs. 2,000 Malpractice or harassment Suspension for 1 to 2 semesters Ragging Immediate suspension and referral to the Anti-Ragging Committee 6. Grievance Redressal

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 2 6.1 Students may submit grievances to the Grievance Redressal Cell through the complaint box or grievance@siet.example.edu. 6.2 The Cell acknowledges a complaint within 3 working days and resolves it within 15 working days. 6.3 Appeals against the Cell's decision may be made to the Principal within 7 days. 7. Anti-Ragging and Internal Complaints 7.1 The Anti-Ragging Committee is chaired by the Principal. Helpline: 1800-XXX-XXXX (24x7). 7.2 The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) handles complaints related to harassment.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 Department Handbook Department: Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) Document No: SIET/CSE/2026/07 | Academic Year: 2026-27 1. About the Department 1.1 The CSE Department was established in 2008 and offers B.E. CSE (intake: 120), M.E. CSE (intake: 18), and Ph.D. programmes. 1.2 Vision: To produce competent computing professionals who contribute to society through innovation and ethical practice. 1.3 Mission: Deliver quality education, promote industry collaboration, and encourage research in emerging areas. 2. Department Leadership Role Contact Head of the Department hod.cse@siet.example.edu Department Coordinator coord.cse@siet.example.edu Class Advisors Assigned section-wise each semester 3. Programme Outcomes and Curriculum 3.1 The B.E. programme is 8 semesters with 160 credits. Students must earn at least 160 credits to graduate. 3.2 The curriculum includes core courses, professional electives, open electives, laboratories, and a final-year project. 3.3 Industry-relevant electives include Machine Learning, Cloud Computing, Cyber Security, and Data Science. 4. Laboratories Laboratory Capacity Timing Programming and Data Structures Lab 60 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM AI and Machine Learning Lab 40 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM

and Data Science. 4. Laboratories Laboratory Capacity Timing Programming and Data Structures Lab 60 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM AI and Machine Learning Lab 40 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM Networks and Cyber Security Lab 40 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM Project and Research Lab 30 Until 6:00 PM with HoD permission 4.1 Lab records must be submitted weekly. Lab internal marks are out of 60 and the external practical exam is out of 40. 4.2 Food and drinks are not allowed in labs. 5. Final-Year Project 5.1 Projects are done in teams of 2 to 4 students under a faculty guide. 5.2 Title approval must be obtained by the end of the 6th semester. 5.3 Reviews: Review-1 (title and literature survey), Review-2 (design and partial implementation), Review-3 (complete implementation), and the final viva. 5.4 Plagiarism must be below 15% in the project report, checked using the college's plagiarism software.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 2 5.5 Students are encouraged to publish a paper in a UGC-care or Scopus-indexed journal or present at a conference. 6. Student Activities 6.1 The CSE Association conducts technical symposiums, hackathons, and workshops every semester. 6.2 Students are encouraged to take MOOCs (NPTEL, Coursera). Up to 2 NPTEL courses of 12 weeks may be credited as open electives. 6.3 Students may earn up to 4 activity points per year through participation in approved events. 7. Mentoring and Support 7.1 Every student is assigned a faculty mentor who meets them at least once a month. 7.2 The mentor tracks attendance, academic performance, and personal concerns, and escalates issues to the HoD when required. 7.3 Remedial classes are conducted for students with CAT marks below 50%. 8. Communication Etiquette 8.1 Official communication with faculty must be through college email IDs or the ERP portal. 8.2 Students may meet the HoD between 3:30 PM and 4:30 PM on working days with prior appointment. 9. Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 Examination Regulations Document No: SIET/EXAM/2026/03 | Controller of Examinations: Office of the CoE 1. Examination Structure 1.1 Each theory course carries 100 marks: 40 internal + 60 external (end-semester). 1.2 Internal assessment: Continuous Assessment Test 1 (CAT-1), CAT-2, assignments, and attendance. 1.3 To pass a course, a student needs a minimum of 40% in the end-semester exam and 50% overall. 2. Internal Assessment Breakdown (40 Marks) Component Marks CAT-1 15 CAT-2 15 Assignments / Mini-project 5 Attendance 5 3. Eligibility to Write End-Semester Exams 3.1 Minimum 75% attendance (or condonation as per the Attendance Rules). 3.2 No pending dues of tuition, hostel, or library fees. 3.3 Registration of all courses on the ERP portal by the stated deadline. 4. Examination Hall Rules 4.1 Students must report to the hall 20 minutes before the exam starts and may not enter after 30 minutes from the start time. 4.2 Carry only the hall ticket, college ID, and permitted stationery. Phones, smartwatches, and notes are prohibited. 4.3 Students must not leave

enter after 30 minutes from the start time. 4.2 Carry only the hall ticket, college ID, and permitted stationery. Phones, smartwatches, and notes are prohibited. 4.3 Students must not leave the hall during the first 45 minutes of the exam. 4.4 Programmable calculators are not allowed unless the question paper states otherwise. 5. Malpractice Offence Penalty Possession of unauthorized material (not used) Warning and cancellation of that paper Copying or use of unauthorized material Cancellation of that paper plus all papers of the semester Impersonation Dismissal from the college and police complaint Misbehavior with invigilators Suspension for 1 year 6. Re-evaluation and Revaluation 6.1 Students may apply for photocopy of the answer script within 5 days of result publication (fee: Rs. 300 per paper). 6.2 Revaluation may be applied within 7 days of publication (fee: Rs. 1,000 per paper). 6.3 Revaluation results are final. 7. Arrear and Supplementary Exams

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 2 7.1 Students with arrears may appear in the next scheduled end-semester exam by paying Rs. 150 per paper. 7.2 Supplementary exams for final-year students are held within 30 days of result publication. 7.3 A student may hold a maximum of 5 arrears to be promoted to the next year. 8. Grading Marks Grade Grade Points 90 to 100 O 10 80 to 89 A+ 9 70 to 79 A 8 60 to 69 B+ 7 50 to 59 B 6 Below 50 RA (Re-appear) 0 9. Medical Absence in Exams 9.1 A student absent due to illness must submit a medical certificate from a registered practitioner within 3 days. A special exam may be permitted at the Principal's discretion.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 Hostel Rules Document No: SIET/HOS/2026/05 | Issued by: Office of the Warden 1. Admission and Allotment 1.1 Hostel admission is based on distance from home (priority to students living beyond 40 km) and availability. 1.2 Rooms are allotted on a sharing basis (2 or 3 students per room). Room change requests need the Warden's approval. 1.3 Students must pay hostel fees (room and mess) at the start of each semester. Late payment attracts a fine of Rs. 100 per day. 2. Timings Activity Timing Hostel entry (weekdays) Before 6:30 PM Hostel entry (weekends) Before 8:00 PM Lights out / silence hours 10:30 PM to 5:30 AM Study hours 7:30 PM to 9:30 PM 1.4 Late entry requires prior written permission from the Warden. Three late entries in a month result in parent intimation. 3. Mess Timings - Breakfast: 7:15 AM to 8:15 AM - Lunch: 12:30 PM to 1:45 PM - Snacks: 4:30 PM to 5:15 PM - Dinner: 7:30 PM to 8:45 PM 3.1 Mess fee is

7:15 AM to 8:15 AM - Lunch: 12:30 PM to 1:45 PM - Snacks: 4:30 PM to 5:15 PM - Dinner: 7:30 PM to 8:45 PM 3.1 Mess fee is Rs. 4,500 per month, charged on a monthly basis. Mess rebate is given only for absence of 5 or more consecutive days with prior notice. 4. Visitors 4.1 Visitors are allowed only in the visitors' room between 4:00 PM and 6:00 PM on Sundays. 4.2 Parents must register in the visitor register. Overnight stay is not permitted. 4.3 Students of the opposite gender are not allowed inside hostel blocks. 5. Out-Pass and Leave 5.1 Students must obtain an out-pass from the Warden to leave the campus during hostel hours. 5.2 Weekend or holiday outings require parental consent by phone or email to the Warden. 5.3 Leaving the hostel for more than 24 hours without informing the Warden is treated as absconding. 6. Prohibited Items and Activities - Cooking appliances (induction stoves, kettles, heaters) in rooms. - Alcohol, tobacco, drugs, and weapons. - Gambling, loud music, and gathering in corridors after

absconding. 6. Prohibited Items and Activities - Cooking appliances (induction stoves, kettles, heaters) in rooms. - Alcohol, tobacco, drugs, and weapons. - Gambling, loud music, and gathering in corridors after lights out. - Two-wheelers and four-wheelers inside the hostel premises without permission.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 2 6.2 Electrical devices beyond a laptop, mobile charger, and fan require the Warden's approval and extra charges. 7. Room Maintenance 7.1 Students must keep rooms clean. Surprise inspections are conducted weekly. 7.2 Damage to furniture or fittings must be paid for by the occupants of the room. 7.3 Students may not hang posters using nails or adhesives on walls. 8. Penalties Violation Penalty Late entry without permission Fine of Rs. 200 Prohibited appliance found Confiscation and fine of Rs. 500 Damage to property Recovery of cost Ragging or violence Immediate expulsion from the hostel Alcohol or drugs Expulsion from the hostel and referral to the Disciplinary Committee 9. Medical Emergencies 9.1 In case of illness, notify the Warden. The campus medical centre is open from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Emergency ambulance service is available 24x7 at 044-XXXX-XXXX.

Types of Leave Type Maximum Duration Approval Authority Casual Leave 2 days at a time, 6 days per semester Class Advisor Medical Leave As per medical certificate HoD On-Duty (OD) As per event HoD Maternity / Special Leave (women students) Up to 60 days Principal Bereavement Leave Up to 7 days HoD 2. Application Procedure 2.1 Apply through the ERP portal or a written leave letter at least 1 day in advance for planned leave. 2.2 For emergencies, parents must inform the Class Advisor by phone or email on the same day. 2.3 Leave for 3 or more days requires a parent's signature on the leave letter. 3. Leave During Examinations 4.1 Leave is not granted during CATs or end-semester exams except for medical emergencies with supporting proof. Section B: Faculty Leave 5. Entitlements (per academic year) Type Days Casual Leave (CL) 12 Earned Leave (EL) 15 (for staff on 12-month contract) Medical Leave 10 days with certificate Maternity Leave 26 weeks (as per statutory provisions) Paternity Leave 10 days Special Casual Leave (conference / FDP) 10 days 5.1 Casual leave cannot be combined with more than 3 consecutive days of other leave without the Principal's approval. 5.2 Faculty must arrange substitution for their classes and get the HoD's approval before taking leave.

Leave Encashment 6.1 Unused EL can be carried forward up to 30 days and encashed at the time of resignation or retirement. 7. Holidays 7.1 The academic calendar lists all public holidays, restricted holidays, and vacation periods. Restricted holidays: any 2 per year may be availed.

Sample Institute of Engineering and Technology (SIET) - Sample document Page 1 Placement Guidelines Document No: SIET/TPC/2026/04 | Issued by: Training and Placement Cell (TPC) 1. Eligibility for Campus Placement 1.1 The student must be a final-year student with no standing arrears at the time of the drive. 1.2 Minimum CGPA of 6.5 (or 65% aggregate) up to the previous semester. Companies may set higher cut-offs. 1.3 Minimum 80% attendance in the previous semester. Students below this are not allowed to sit for drives. 1.4 The student must register with the TPC portal by 31 July of the final year. 2. One Student, One Offer Policy Offer Category Salary Package Rule Dream Rs. 8 LPA and above May attend further drives only for higher packages Super Dream Rs. 12 LPA and above Not eligible for any more drives except by special permission Regular Below Rs. 8 LPA May attend one Dream or Super Dream drive after 2.1 A student who is placed in a Regular company can attend a Dream drive, but not another Regular drive. 2.2 Students who decline

Dream or Super Dream drive after 2.1 A student who is placed in a Regular company can attend a Dream drive, but not another Regular drive. 2.2 Students who decline an offer after accepting it are debarred from further placement activity. 3. Pre-Placement Training 3.1 Mandatory training in aptitude, communication, and technical skills begins in the 5th semester. 3.2 Attendance in pre-placement training is compulsory. Students with less than 85% attendance may be barred from drives. 3.3 Mock interviews and group discussions are conducted in the 6th and 7th semesters. 4. Drive-Day Discipline 4.1 Students must wear formal attire and carry resume copies, ID card, and photo ID. 4.2 Students must report 30 minutes before the scheduled time. Late students are not allowed in. 4.3 Mobile phones must be switched off during tests and interviews. 4.4 Any misconduct during a drive may lead to a ban from all future drives. 5. 5. Internships 5.1 Internships of 4 to 8 weeks are encouraged during the summer after the 6th semester. 5.2 Students must get prior approval from the HoD and submit an internship report with a completion certificate. 5.3 Internship OD attendance is capped at 15 days per semester. 6. Higher Studies and Entrepreneurship 6.1 Students opting out of placement for higher studies must submit a written declaration to the TPC. 6.2 Students running a startup may seek exemption from placement with approval from the Principal.
